title: Quantum-hardware spectral co-design framework for multifrequency Rydberg electrometry
authors: Song Huang, Guibin Tian, Fernando Quijandría, Zhengjiang Li, Zhimin He, Franco Nori, Yong Lu
abstract: Engineering electromagnetic hardware to satisfy discrete quantum-defined spectral constraints constitutes a general spectral co-design problem for quantum systems. Here we address this challenge in multifrequency Rydberg electrometry by directly coupling a fabrication-constrained simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation (SPSA)--Adam optimizer to full-wave finite-element eigenmode simulations. Requiring neither analytical nor adjoint gradients, the method operates over a discrete design space containing approximately $10^{300}$-configurations and yields a novel multimode electrometry architecture that simultaneously aligns four high-$Q$ eigenmodes with four selected Cs Rydberg transitions. The optimized design remains highly robust to fabrication imperfections, achieving a relative frequency error as low as $8.42\times10^{-7}$ while reducing the device length by a factor of $1.75\times10^{2}$, thereby overcoming the difficulty of simultaneous multimode spectral matching encountered in conventional design. For a comparable simulation budget, the proposed co-design framework achieves frequency-matching errors approximately 10 and 41 times smaller than those of covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy and discrete simulated annealing, respectively. The electrometry is predicted to provide an average input-power-sensitivity enhancement of approximately $4.04\times10^{3}$, demonstrating quantum--hardware spectral co-design as a general route toward compact hardware for multichannel quantum sensing.
summary: The authors present a quantum-hardware spectral co-design framework to engineer microwave cavities for high-precision Rydberg electrometry. By coupling a specialized SPSA–Adam optimizer to full-wave FEM simulations, they successfully tuned the cavity to simultaneously match four distinct quantum transition frequencies. This method yields a highly robust, compact, and significantly more sensitive sensing architecture than previously achieved.
main_problem: The paper addresses the general spectral co-design problem: engineering electromagnetic hardware to precisely match discrete, quantum-defined spectral constraints for multi-frequency quantum sensing.
main_result: A novel co-design framework was developed that successfully aligned four high-Q cavity eigenmodes with target Cs Rydberg transitions, achieving extremely low frequency errors and significantly enhancing input-power sensitivity.
method: The optimization uses a simulator-in-the-loop approach, coupling a Constrained Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation (SPSA)–Adam optimizer to full-wave finite-element eigenmode simulations.
model_or_system: The physical system is a copper cavity structure designed for multifrequency Rydberg electrometry using Cesium (Cs) atoms. The geometry is parameterized by an 85-dimensional vector, and the objective is to minimize the frequency mismatch between the cavity modes and four selected Rydberg transition frequencies.
key_observables: Relative frequency error (achieved as low as $8.42 	imes 10^{-7}$), input-power-sensitivity enhancement ($\approx 4.04 	imes 10^3$), and the total frequency mismatch ($\Delta f$).
important_parameters: Four target Cs Rydberg transitions (e.g., 3.0572 THz), the 85-dimensional design vector $\mathbf{x}$, and the fabrication tolerance ($\Delta_{	ext{tol}}$).
main_assumptions: The optimization relies on the ability to repeatedly call a full-wave finite-element simulator (COMSOL) within the optimization loop, and the process involves approximations like SPSA gradient estimation and quantization to a fabrication grid.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy level diagram for the excitation scheme and the optimization process, showing the convergence of the SPSA–Adam method compared to CMA-ES and DSA baselines.
paper_structure: The paper details the formulation of the spectral co-design problem, introduces the SPSA–Adam optimization protocol, presents the results of optimizing the geometry for four channels, and concludes by comparing its performance against established optimization benchmarks.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, generalizable computational methodology for designing quantum hardware. The coupling of advanced optimization techniques (SPSA-Adam) directly to complex physical simulators (FEM) is highly relevant for realizing next-generation quantum devices.

(a) Energy level diagram for a Cs atom, driven by 852-nm probe, 1470-nm dressing, and 779-nm coupling fields. Four selected cavity modes are designed to align with four microwave transitions shown in the inset as four different waves. (b) Constrained SPSA–Adam optimization for an 85-parameter geometry x(t). Two-point SPSA evaluations x± = x(t) ± ϵ ∆(t) are simulated with a COMSOL eigenfrequency solver to obtain four-mode outputs f(x±); the normalized objective L yields a stochastic gradient estimate used by Adam. The update is projected onto a fabrication feasible set to produce x(t+1).
